name: v2.7 D3 Hostile Canonical Verification
description: Verify only a canonical root cause after built-in semantic deduplication; no PoC work at this stage.
content:
Repository: {{repo_full}} at commit {{commit_sha}}. Scope: {{repo_scope}}. Dependencies: {{dependencies}}. Configuration: {{configuration}}.
Canonical candidate: {{summary}}. Claimed type: {{vulnerability_type}}. Fault: {{file_path}}:{{line}}.
Actor: {{malicious_actor}}. Claimed trigger: {{malicious_input_example}}. Trace: {{trigger_flow}}.
Explanation and root-cause fingerprint: {{explanation}}.
Re-read every cited production operation and attacker-to-impact hop at the pinned commit. Try to disprove the candidate using dominating guards, authorization and interceptors, default deployment configuration, DB constraints, transaction/lock semantics, recovery paths, and intended behavior. Use a negative-control hypothesis. Check known issues/audits and exact program scope only when evidence is available. Do not build or run a PoC here.
Return exactly one verdict: confirmed, plausible_needs_poc, known_duplicate, out_of_scope, configuration_only, privileged_only, false_positive, or insufficient_evidence. confirmed means source-level proof of the complete trigger and concrete impact, still requiring D4 reproduction. plausible_needs_poc means a concrete fault and plausible impact with a named fact requiring reproduction. Do not rescue speculation with this label. Identify the least-privileged actor, existing guard, first unsupported hop, source evidence, impact, and remaining deployment/scope facts. Reject an unreachable or guarded candidate before D4.
